pyre_plant_distribution_correct.text: every wild plant on a fresh Pyrelands map is ember grass, quick grass or scorch-fruit; no other wild plant species grows there.

pyre_animal_distribution_correct.text: every wild animal on a fresh Pyrelands map belongs to the biome's fire-ecology cast, no other kind wanders in, and the small common grazers outnumber the big predators.

pyre_mapgen_log_clean.text: generating a fresh Pyrelands map raises no error message on screen.

pyre_ground_deep_ash.text: a fresh Pyrelands map is almost all deep ash; only small pockets of unburned soil and gravel remain, and standing water is ringed with richer ground.

pyre_ash_fertile_when_watered.text: a crop on deep ash beside a watered channel grows clearly faster than the same crop on dry ash.

pyre_fresh_burn_feeds_the_field.text: ground that has just burned grows noticeably faster for a few days, and a black rain washes that advantage away early.

pyre_grass_chokes_ground.text: open ground is carpeted densely in grass; there are no bare-dirt expanses where grass should carry the ground.

pyre_embergrass_regrows.text: a burned patch of grass is visibly re-greening within a few days and largely green again within about a week, at the biome's own heat.

pyre_burn_line_present.text: a fresh Pyrelands map shows an active line of fire somewhere, with a visibly scorched trail behind its advancing front.

pyre_scorchfruit_fire_born.text: scorch-fruit appears only on freshly burned ground, never as ordinary wild growth on unburned land.

pyre_scorchfruit_produces.text: a ripe scorch-fruit plant yields edible fruit that a colonist can harvest, and eating it raises a hungry colonist's food meter.

pyre_scorchfruit_spoils_fast.text: unrefrigerated, harvested scorch-fruit rots within about four days, and a ripe unharvested plant withers within about a day.

pyre_ruins_scorched.text: ruins on a fresh Pyrelands map stand blackened and fire-scarred, not pristine.

pyre_fulgurite_after_lightning.text: after a dry-lightning storm strikes sandy ground, at least one impact site bears a visible lump of fulgurite glass.

pyre_firehawk_carries_ember.text: a fire-hawk picks up a burning twig and a new fire starts where it drops it, ahead of the existing blaze.

pyre_furnacebeast_warmth.text: a pawn standing in the open near a furnace-beast shows a readable warmth status that disappears after it walks away.

pyre_furnacebeast_heats_room.text: an enclosed room holding a furnace-beast becomes clearly hotter than a comparable room without one.

pyre_burrowers_dive.text: when fire reaches a burrowing grazer it shows a readable burrowed status and comes through unharmed once the fire has passed.

pyre_ashfall_darkens_drifts.text: ash fall dims the map and lays visible loose-ash drifts that keep accumulating while it lasts.

pyre_cinderfall_distinct.text: cinderfall is recognisable at a glance as its own weather, not ash fall renamed.

pyre_blackrain_reads.text: black rain falls visibly dark, plainly different from ordinary blue-grey rain.

pyre_cannot_ordinary_rain.text: ordinary rain falling on a Pyrelands map; its only wet weather is black rain.
